title: AI Operating Model and Center of Excellence

questions.question: When does AI work need an operating model?
options: When ownership, standards, reusable assets, or scaling governance are unclear
Only when there is one small prompt
Only when no team uses AI
questions.explanation: Operating models help scale AI work across teams.

questions.question: Which signal is part of this lesson?
questions.explanation: Reuse opportunity indicates that assets and standards may need governance.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A ranked operating-model plan with governance controls
questions.explanation: The artifact recommends role, standards, asset, and governance controls.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
questions.explanation: Asset registries support reuse and governance.

questions.question: When is Center of Excellence service design appropriate?
options: When scale value and governance complexity are high enough to justify reusable services
Only when no standards are needed
Only when ownership is already irrelevant
questions.explanation: CoE service design is useful when scaling AI across teams.

questions.question: What should an AI operating model clarify?
options: Role charter, standards backlog, asset registry, and governance cadence
questions.explanation: These controls make scaling practical and maintainable.
